I'm an undergraduate at Penn State — computer science with minors in physics and AI, Schreyer Honors College — working toward a career in mechanistic interpretability research. I came up through physics: my first real project was a [Monte Carlo radiative-transfer code](../posts/where-the-error-hides/) for neutron-star atmospheres, the kind of work where nothing counts until it matches an exact answer. Transformers get the same treatment here: I trained a small character-level model and [traced a half-built copying mechanism in its weights](../posts/induction-head/), read [GPT-2's IOI circuit through three methods](../posts/ioi-circuit/) to see where each one goes blind, traced [the J-lens offset to the model's own token frequency](../posts/jlens-offset/), and am currently developing measures for internal monitoring when a model's chain of thought becomes illegible. Everything on this site is built or measured by me — controls included, especially the ones that broke my own hypotheses.
